chapter: Hampton band, Honolulu and the war years
title: San Francisco, Carl Johnson's band and the shipyard
summary: He returns to Los Angeles in October 1942, joins Carl Johnson, and is let go after falling asleep from shipyard work by day.

blocks.x: So I rushed back to San Francisco; I was there three months.
Did you work any during that time in San Francisco?
No. I think I had about a half a dozen gigs. Finally I figured that wasn't the place for me and I ended up back in Los Angeles, in October, 1942.
I found a job playing my horn immediately; that's when I was with Carl Johnson.
Yes, you were with the Carl Johnson Orchestra.
Carl Johnson was the son of Spencer Johnson, who was at one time the president of the then Local 767.
How long did you stay with him?
Oh, maybe a couple of months. I was with him at the time that I went to work at the shipyard.
Tell us about your experience with him.
Working at the shipyard everyday and getting home at six o'clock at night and had to be at work at eight and work until one o'clock in the morning.

One time Carl was knocking off the band and instead of me playing, I was sitting there asleep. So Carl let me go; he said it was better if you go because it was too much for you working daytime and night too. It tickled me (laughter).
Like burning the candle at both ends.
But then I guess at that time a lot of musicians were working in the defense plants and playing gigs at night.
